meta.name: Salesforce Certified Administrator (ADM-201)
meta.notes: Initial Salesforce Administrator (ADM-201) pack — covers Profiles vs Permission Sets, Org-Wide Defaults, Role Hierarchy, Validation Rules, Record Types, Flow, Approval Processes, Sandbox types, Data Loader vs Import Wizard, Report Formats, Field-Level Security, and Sharing Rules. Balanced answer key (3/3/3/3).

questions.question: All users in an org have the Sales User profile, but a small group of regional managers temporarily need access to an additional custom object during a pilot. The admin wants to grant this access without cloning or modifying the profile. Which approach fits best?
options: Create a new profile that includes the extra access and reassign the managers to it
Edit the Sales User profile to add the access for everyone
Assign a permission set granting the extra access to the regional managers
Add the managers to a public group that owns the custom object records
questions.explanation: Permission sets extend a user's access on top of their profile without changing the profile itself, which makes them the right tool for granting additional permissions to a subset of users. Creating a new profile means duplicating maintenance, editing the shared profile grants access to everyone, and public groups control record sharing — not object/field permissions like Create or Read on a custom object.

questions.question: An admin wants to make the Opportunity object private by default so users only see opportunities they own or that are explicitly shared with them. Which setting controls this baseline visibility?
options: Organization-Wide Default (OWD) sharing setting on Opportunity
The Standard User profile's Opportunity object permissions
A criteria-based sharing rule on Opportunity
The role hierarchy 'Grant Access Using Hierarchies' checkbox
questions.explanation: Organization-Wide Defaults define the most restrictive baseline of record-level access for each object — setting Opportunity's OWD to Private means users only see records they own (or that are shared via roles, rules, teams, or manual sharing). Profiles control object/field CRUD, not record visibility; sharing rules open access back up after OWD restricts it; and the hierarchy checkbox just propagates access upward, it does not set the baseline.

questions.question: With Opportunity OWD set to Private and 'Grant Access Using Hierarchies' enabled, which users can see an opportunity owned by a Sales Rep in the West region?
options: Only the Sales Rep who owns the record
The owning Sales Rep and every user above them in the role hierarchy
Every user in the West region regardless of role
Only system administrators
questions.explanation: When OWD is Private and hierarchy access is on, the record owner sees their own record and so does anyone above them in the role hierarchy (their manager, the VP, etc.). Peers in the same role do not automatically see it; admins do because of 'Modify All Data,' but the question is about hierarchy behavior in general.

questions.question: Sales leadership requires that an Opportunity cannot be saved with Stage = 'Closed Won' unless the Amount field is greater than zero. Which Salesforce feature enforces this at save time with a custom error message?
options: A Workflow Rule with a Field Update action
A Flow triggered after save that updates the Amount
A Process Builder that posts a Chatter message
A Validation Rule whose formula blocks the save
questions.explanation: Validation rules evaluate a formula on save and, when the formula returns TRUE, block the save and display a custom error message — exactly what's needed here. Workflow Rules and Process Builder are retired automation tools that don't block saves with errors, and a Flow that runs after save can't prevent the original save from completing.

questions.question: A company sells both consumer products and enterprise services and needs different picklist values, page layouts, and sales processes on the Opportunity object for each line of business. Which Salesforce feature supports this within a single object?
options: Record Types, each with its own picklist values, page layout, and sales process
A separate custom Opportunity object for each line of business
Field-Level Security on the existing Opportunity fields
Profile-based page layout assignments without record types
questions.explanation: Record Types let one object support multiple business processes — each record type maps to its own picklist value subset, page layout (per profile), and sales process. Creating a separate custom object loses standard Opportunity functionality and reporting; field-level security only hides fields; and assigning layouts by profile alone can't vary picklist values or sales processes per record.

questions.question: Salesforce has retired Workflow Rules and Process Builder for new automations. Which tool is the recommended replacement for building point-and-click automations that run when records are created or updated?
options: Apex triggers written by a developer
Flow (specifically a Record-Triggered Flow)
A scheduled report subscription
A new Workflow Rule cloned from an existing one
questions.explanation: Flow is now the strategic, point-and-click automation tool in Salesforce, and Record-Triggered Flows specifically run on create/update of a record — replacing the retired Workflow Rules and Process Builder. Apex requires code (and isn't 'point-and-click'), reports don't perform automations, and Salesforce has stopped allowing new Workflow Rules to be created in most orgs.

questions.question: When an Opportunity Amount exceeds $250,000 it must be reviewed by the VP of Sales before the record can move to 'Closed Won.' The reviewer must explicitly approve or reject, with the record locked in the meantime. Which feature should the admin configure?
options: A validation rule that blocks the stage change when Amount exceeds the threshold
A scheduled report sent to the VP listing large opportunities
An Approval Process with entry criteria on Amount and the VP as the approver
A queue that owns all large opportunities until they are reviewed
questions.explanation: An Approval Process is purpose-built for this: entry criteria (Amount > 250k) submit the record, the record is locked, the assigned approver (VP) explicitly Approves or Rejects, and configured actions run on each outcome. A validation rule can block a save but doesn't capture an approver decision or lock the record, scheduled reports are passive, and a queue changes ownership without enforcing review.

questions.question: Before a major release, the team needs an exact, near-real-time copy of production — schema plus all data — to perform full regression testing. Which sandbox type fits this requirement?
options: Developer sandbox (metadata only, ~200 MB)
Developer Pro sandbox (metadata only, ~1 GB)
Partial Copy sandbox (metadata plus a sample of data)
Full sandbox (metadata plus all production data)
questions.explanation: A Full sandbox is the only type that copies all production data and metadata, making it the right environment for full regression and performance testing. Developer and Developer Pro copy metadata only, and a Partial Copy sandbox includes just a sample of data defined by a sandbox template — neither matches the 'exact copy' requirement.

questions.question: An admin must load 600,000 Account records from a CSV exported by the legacy CRM into Salesforce. Which tool is most appropriate, and why?
options: Data Loader — supports up to 5 million records per load and runs against standard and custom objects
Data Import Wizard — handles any record volume on every standard object
Mass Transfer Records — designed specifically for bulk CSV imports
Manual entry through the Account list view
questions.explanation: Data Loader handles up to 5 million records in a single operation and works with all standard and custom objects, so it fits a 600k-record Account load. The Data Import Wizard is capped at 50,000 records per import and only supports a subset of objects. Mass Transfer Records changes ownership of existing records — it does not import new ones. Manual entry is impractical at this volume.

questions.question: A sales manager wants a report that shows opportunities grouped by Stage with subtotals of Amount per stage, displayed as a single column of groups. Which report format should the admin choose?
options: Tabular — a simple list of rows with no groupings or subtotals
Summary — rows grouped by one or more fields with subtotals
Matrix — rows grouped by one field and columns grouped by another
Joined — multiple report blocks of different report types side by side
questions.explanation: Summary reports group rows by one or more fields and display subtotals at each grouping level — perfect for opportunities grouped by Stage with Amount subtotals. Tabular reports are flat lists without groupings, Matrix reports cross-tabulate by both rows and columns, and Joined reports combine multiple report blocks (often of different report types).

questions.question: HR needs the Compensation field on the Employee object to be invisible to standard users but editable for the HR Manager profile. Where should the admin configure this?
options: Org-Wide Defaults — set Employee to Private
Page layout — remove the field from the layout assigned to standard users
Field-Level Security on the Compensation field, varied by profile (or via a permission set)
A validation rule that prevents non-HR users from saving changes to Compensation
questions.explanation: Field-Level Security (FLS) controls per-profile (and per-permission-set) visibility and editability of individual fields across the UI, API, reports, and list views — it is the only setting that truly hides the value everywhere from users who shouldn't see it. OWD governs records, not fields. Removing a field from a page layout hides it on that layout but leaves it exposed in reports/API. A validation rule blocks saves but doesn't hide the value.

questions.question: Account OWD is Private. The CFO needs all users in the 'Finance' public group to read every Account where Industry = 'Banking,' without changing OWD or the role hierarchy. What should the admin configure?
options: An owner-based sharing rule that shares all Accounts owned by any user with the Finance group
A new role above the current hierarchy and place Finance users in it
Manual sharing on each Banking account, one record at a time
A criteria-based sharing rule where Industry equals 'Banking,' shared with the Finance public group as Read Only
questions.explanation: Criteria-based sharing rules open access to records that match field criteria (Industry = 'Banking') by sharing them with a group, role, or territory — exactly the requirement here. Owner-based sharing would share by owner, not by Industry. Restructuring the hierarchy is invasive and would grant access to other records too. Manual sharing doesn't scale and isn't automatic for new Banking accounts.
